integrity: The proof reconstructs the exact gradient and converts global seam orthogonality into a reciprocal identity on two positive simplices. Varying two coordinates forces each sign class of the hyperplane normal to be a singleton, after which the weight ratio is exact. The converse is checked directly. A standalone checker verifies the gradient identities on many dimensions and weights; finite tests are consistency checks, not the proof of the infinite statement.
scientific_limitations: The theorem classifies only linear hyperplanes through the origin for the positive-weight weighted geometric-mean antinorm. It does not classify all self-dual antinorms, does not treat weaker local seam conditions, and does not resolve the open non-admissible splitting problem for autopolar conic polyhedra. An unindexed equivalent observation remains a residual originality risk because the proof is elementary once the explicit gradient is known.
title: Rigidity of orthogonal seams for weighted geometric-mean antinorms
